findings.title: Unknown WMI permanent event subscription
findings.description: A permanent WMI event subscription was observed.
findings.rationale: Permanent WMI subscriptions are uncommon and historically used for persistence.
findings.recommendation: Validate filter/consumer legitimacy and change control records.

findings.title: Service executable in unexpected writable location
findings.description: A service references an executable whose directory appears writable by non-administrators.
findings.rationale: Writable service binary directories enable persistence via binary replacement.
findings.recommendation: Validate directory ACLs and recent modifications in the service path.

findings.title: Autorun entry references missing target
findings.description: A Run key or startup folder entry references a file that is not present.
findings.rationale: Broken autorun entries can reflect removed malware or incomplete cleanup.
findings.recommendation: Correlate with recent file metadata and login timelines.

findings.title: Process executing from temporary directory
findings.description: A running process image path resides under a temporary or user-writable directory.
findings.rationale: Legitimate software rarely runs persistently from temp paths; this may indicate staging.
findings.recommendation: Review process parent chain, signer metadata, and network connections for the same PID.

findings.title: Scheduled task references missing executable
findings.description: A scheduled task action points to a path that does not exist.
findings.rationale: Missing task targets may indicate cleanup after execution or dormant tasks.
findings.recommendation: Inspect task definition and last run times.

findings.title: Listening service on all interfaces
findings.description: A network listener is bound to all interfaces rather than localhost.
findings.rationale: Broad listeners increase remote exposure; verify intended exposure.
findings.recommendation: Map owning process and firewall policy for the listener port.

findings.title: Recently created persistence metadata
findings.description: Persistence metadata indicates a very recent creation timestamp.
findings.rationale: Recent persistence changes deserve timeline correlation during triage.
findings.recommendation: Compare creation time with case timeline and change tickets.
